conventions.convention: Loss is nonnegative and may equal infinity. Pointwise risk requires measurable action sections, but no measurable structure on the parameter set.
Domination means weak improvement at every parameter and strict improvement at at least one parameter; admissibility compares against all decision rules in the same problem.

Bayes risk requires a parameter-measurable model kernel and jointly measurable loss. Minimax value takes the infimum over measurable randomized rules. Parameter and action spaces are nonempty; extrema use the extended-real order and need not be attained.

Integral Jensen assumes AC and Countable Choice, dimension at least one, a nonempty closed convex Borel action set, finite first moment, and a barycenter in that set. Extended convexity uses the endpoint convention 0 times infinity equals zero.
The finite-moment and in-action-set barycenter condition holds almost surely under each sampling law. One measurable rule is constructed using the measurable good set and a fixed fallback action.

The Bayes theorem assumes AC, standard-Borel parameter and data spaces, and a supplied measurable deterministic minimizer. Its posterior inequality holds for every action on one measurable data-marginal full-measure set.

load_bearing.statement: For a statistical experiment, a measurable action space, nonnegative loss with measurable action sections, and a randomized decision kernel, risk is the iterated nonnegative loss integral against the action kernel and sampling law. No measurability on the parameter set is required.

Under the stated parameter-kernel and joint-loss measurability hypotheses, Bayes risk is the prior integral of risk; worst-case risk is its parameter supremum; minimax value is the infimum of worst-case risk over measurable randomized rules. A minimax rule attains that infimum.

For measurable parameter and data spaces, a probability prior, and a probability model kernel, J(C) = ∫ K(θ,Cθ) π(dθ) defines a product-space probability measure. Every nonnegative product-measurable function satisfies the stated iterated-kernel integral identity.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. For d ≥ 1, a nonempty closed convex C ⊆ Rᵈ, a Borel probability μ with finite first moment and coordinatewise barycenter b ∈ C, and a Borel measurable convex f:C→[0,+∞], one has f(b) ≤ ∫ f dμ.

Under AC, standard-Borel parameter and data spaces, a probability model kernel, a prior, and jointly measurable nonnegative loss, a measurable deterministic rule attaining the posterior minimum for every action on one measurable data-marginal full-measure set minimizes prior-integrated risk among all randomized decision rules.
A rule dominates another when its risk is no larger at every parameter and strictly smaller at at least one parameter. A rule is admissible if no decision rule dominates it.

seams_checked.note: Read the prerequisite page and the randomized-procedure, action-law, and estimator items. Uses preserve pointwise probability kernels, eventwise data measurability, parameter-independent procedures, and the absence of a random-seed representation assumption.

Read the prerequisite page and both experiment and parameter-kernel definitions. Pointwise risk uses only individual sampling laws; prior integration separately invokes the measurable parameter-kernel structure.

The page and def-bias-and-mean-squared-error preserve possibly infinite squared-error risk, while restricting bias to integrable estimators. They explicitly avoid imposing parameter measurability for pointwise risk.

Read the page, lem-test-zero-one-loss-risk-identities, and def-test-size-and-power. Binary loss sections are measurable and nonnegative; null risk is rejection probability and alternative risk is its complement. No parameter measurability is inferred.

Read the page and the Le Cam, Assouad, and Fano consumers. Their finite parameter spaces support the measurable-model and joint-loss hypotheses. Lower bounds apply to arbitrary randomized kernels before taking the infimum of maximum risks.

Read the page and six risk consumers. They use expected squared fitted-value loss, distinguish probability bounds from expectation bounds, and state the deterministic Borel estimator class explicitly for their Gaussian-sequence minimax comparison.

Read the page and M/Z definitions. This is a contextual page prerequisite: empirical criteria may be signed and are defined separately, without being identified with the supplier's nonnegative decision loss or posterior-risk minimization.
The page and def-pointwise-regression-risk correctly specialize pointwise risk to a fixed real regression target and a measurable real estimator, allowing infinity without a finite-moment assumption.

Read the page and thm-series-training-risk. Its scope note explicitly treats expected empirical training-design loss as a separately defined criterion and does not identify it with independent test risk or directly import the parameter/action risk definition.

Read the page, robust-risk and modulus definitions, and Huber lower-bound theorem. They retain target-first nonnegative loss with measurable action sections, introduce the parameter action-space structure explicitly, and keep expected and tail risk distinct.
